expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response explains that on AL2023 (sqlite backend), rpm --rebuilddb only rebuilds the index from existing headers, and since the error indicated total corruption ('file is not a database'), there were no headers left, resulting in an empty but valid database. It correctly recommends backing up /var/lib/rpm, running rpm --initdb, then reinstalling system-release first, then '*' with --skip-broken, followed by dnf distro-sync. It also explicitly notes that re-running rpm --rebuilddb again would be a no-op/destructive and cannot recover this total-loss case. This matches all the key points of the expected output.
expected_output.evidence: "rpm --rebuilddb only *rebuilds the index from existing package headers*. When the error was \"file is not a database\" — i.e., total corruption, not just a stale/locked index — there were no headers left to rebuild from... rm -f /var/lib/rpm/rpmdb.sqlite*... rpm --initdb... dnf -y install system-release... dnf -y reinstall '*' --skip-broken... dnf -y distro-sync --skip-broken... don't fall back to deleting /var/lib/rpm outright or re-running plain rpm --rebuilddb again — both are no-ops or destructive here since the headers are already confirmed gone."

assertion_results.text: Explains that rpm --rebuilddb leaves an empty database because there are no on-disk headers to rebuild from when the sqlite file is totally corrupt
assertion_results.evidence: The output states: 'rpm --rebuilddb only rebuilds the index from existing package headers.
